summary: He, she, him, her, and it are all one sign in ASL: a point to the side, toward the person or toward a spot you've set up for them.
steps: Point to the side, toward the person you mean, or toward the spot in the air you've assigned them.
If gender matters, establish it first with MAN, WOMAN, or a fingerspelled name, then point.
Keep pointing to the same spot every time you mean that person.
note: Assign each person you're talking about a spot in the space in front of you. Your sister on the right, your boss on the left. From then on, a point to the right means your sister. That's how ASL tracks 'he said, she said' with no confusion.
mistakes: Looking for a different sign for 'she' or 'her.' There isn't one. Location and context carry it.

faq.q: How do I show that I mean 'she' instead of 'he'?
faq.a: Set it up first: sign WOMAN or fingerspell the name, then point to a spot. After that, pointing to that spot means her.
